About OfficeSpace:

OfficeSpace Software provides the leading AI operating system for the built world, that helps teams plan, connect, and perform in the workplace. As a performance-based, PE-backed company, we hire based on merit and a willingness to do what it takes to succeed long-term. You’re a great fit for the role if you’re entrepreneurial, passionate, motivated by building at light speed, and an Agentic AI early adopter. Our world-class teams operate in the US, Canada, and Costa Rica in a culture of trust, respect, growth, and impact.

We're looking for a hands-on operations leader to own the intersection of Deal Operations and GTM Systems, translating go-to-market strategy into the processes, governance, and tooling that let the field execute efficiently.

This role leads the Deal Operations team through the full order-to-contract lifecycle, including quoting, pricing, deal desk, and renewals, while directing the Systems team's stewardship of our GTM tech stack (Salesforce, Gong, Accord, DealHub and more). You'll serve as the connective tissue between Finance, Sales leadership, and the systems and operations teams that support them, owning the governance frameworks, operating rhythms, and tool access controls that keep the GTM engine running smoothly.

This is a people-leadership role for someone who combines strong Salesforce and deal-ops expertise with an eye toward automation and AI-assisted workflows, ideally with experience in a PE-backed or high-growth SaaS environment. Reports to the SVP, Finance & RevOps. Remote (U.S.).

Responsibilities

GTM Strategy Execution

  • Partner with Sales leadership, ELT and SLT to execute on GTM strategy and insights and translate them into operational processes the field and systems can execute against.
  • Own the governance framework for how strategy decisions flow into systems and field processes. Ensure policies are well documented.
  • Serve as the cross-functional bridge between Finance, Sales leadership, Deal Operations and GTM systems, ensuring alignment and clean handoffs.
  • Partner with enablement to drive seller productivity, workflow optimization, and manager support.
  • Own the operational handoff between deal operations and Finance's cash collections process, serving as the escalation point for deal structure or contract terms that impact billings or collections.

Operations Planning

  • Own RevOps ticket queue and ensure tickets and requests are triaged appropriately.
  • Design and document the operating rhythms and governance processes that keep GTM Systems and Deal Ops running smoothly.
  • Govern GTM tool access and AI credit utilization by maintaining user access controls across the tech stack, conducting regular access audits, and monitoring AI tool consumption to ensure spend stays within budget.
  • Stay ahead of the stack by evaluating tooling, directing integrations, and championing AI-assisted workflows where they create real leverage.
  • Oversee any contractor relationships ensuring high-quality partnership and adherence to budget.

Deal Operations Oversight

  • Oversee the Deal Operations team through the full order-to-contract process, including pricing operations, quoting and deal desk.
  • Manage renewals end-to-end lifecycle, including owning the handoff from executed contracts to Finance for cash collections, ensuring clean data transfer, timing alignment, and resolution of any billing or collections issues that trace back to deal structure.
  • Support the field with deal-related issues and provide managers with ad hoc operational support, such as campaign contact lists and field-facing resources.
  • Own the governance of deal approval processes, ensuring deal structure issues are flagged and escalated appropriately.
  • Lead close-of-period process, including confirming bookings accuracy and partnering with Finance on period-end reconciliation.
  • Identify and drive automation opportunities across the entire order-to-cash process to reduce manual load and increase cycle speed.

Systems Team Oversight

  • Direct the Systems team lead and team in owning and evolving the GTM tech stack, including Salesforce, Gong, Accord, DealHub and other related systems as well as roadmap ownership and prioritization.
  • Ensure the stack is integrated, healthy, and not creating friction for the field.
  • Oversee field triage for system issues and ensure recurring issues are addressed upstream in process or configuration.

Qualifications

Experience and Skills

  • 8 to 12 years in Revenue Operations, GTM Operations, or a closely related function with a track record of translating strategy into field-ready operational processes.
  • Ability to partner with and communicate across GTM leadership, translating strategy and insights into actionable processes and system requirements.
  • Proven people leader with a track record of developing talent and driving team performance.
  • Experience in a PE-backed or high-growth SaaS environment.
  • Strong Salesforce expertise to evaluate architectural decisions, identify configuration optimizations, and serve as a business partner to technical teammates, translating GTM strategy into system requirements they can execute against.
  • Solid command of deal operations mechanics including quoting, CPQ, deal desk approval workflows, and renewal management.
  • AI-curious mindset with awareness of where AI and automation are going in GTM and the ability to direct a technically strong team toward high-leverage automations with a drive to build toward a more automated revenue operations function.

Why OfficeSpace?

  • High-Performance Culture: At OfficeSpace, we believe in the power of accountability, focus, and drive. Our A-Player team members work together to deliver measurable, meaningful results. We recognize and reward those who push boundaries and achieve excellence.
  • Ownership and Accountability: We trust our employees to take full ownership of their roles, providing the autonomy to innovate and the support to succeed. We seek individuals who are self-motivated and thrive in an environment where they can drive impactful outcomes.
  • Technology-Forward: As a company invested in cutting-edge technology, we integrate AI and other advanced solutions across our platform to enhance productivity, customer experience, and process efficiency. Our team members are excited by the potential of AI and proactively explore ways it can drive our success.
  • Growth Mindset: Continuous learning and improvement are integral to our culture. We encourage our team to embrace challenges, seek knowledge, and develop both personally and professionally.

jobs.description:
About Us

LexisNexis Legal & Professional serves customers across the global legal market with leading information, analytics, and technology solutions. We support law firms, corporate legal departments, and government entities in advancing the rule of law and improving legal outcomes.

Our Legal Market business is focused on innovation, commercial growth, and delivering exceptional customer value. We are seeking an experienced Senior HR Manager / Senior Human Resources Business Partner to provide strategic and operational HR partnership to leaders and employees while supporting an evolving and diverse workforce.


About the Role

The Senior HR Manager / Senior Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP) serves as a trusted advisor to business leaders, managers, and employees, providing practical and strategic HR guidance that supports business priorities, workforce effectiveness, employee engagement, and organizational performance.


This role will support a workforce consisting of both union-represented and non-union employees and requires demonstrated experience in labor and employee relations. The Senior HR Manager will advise leaders on complex employee matters, grievances, performance and conduct issues, organizational change, and the consistent application of company policies and collective bargaining agreements.


The role partners closely with specialized HR teams including Talent Acquisition, Employee Experience, Talent Development, Total Rewards, Employee Relations, Legal, and HR Operations to deliver integrated HR solutions. The successful candidate will combine strong business acumen with hands-on HR expertise and will be comfortable operating in a complex, fast-paced environment. The role requires sound judgment, strong negotiation and influencing capabilities, and the ability to build trusted relationships with business leaders, employees, union representatives, and HR stakeholders.


Key Responsibilities


Business Partnership

  • Partner with business leaders and managers to understand business priorities and translate them into practical people plans and HR solutions.
  • Provide coaching, consultation, and HR guidance to leaders and managers on workforce, talent, performance, organizational, and employee matters.
  • Use workforce data and HR insights to identify trends, risks, and opportunities and support informed business decision-making.
  • Support organizational changes, restructures, workforce initiatives, and business transformation efforts.
  • Partner with HR Centers of Excellence to implement enterprise and regional programs while adapting solutions to meet local business and workforce needs.
  • Promote AI fluency and support adoption of AI-enabled ways of working across the workforce.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen workforce skills and capabilities in support of evolving business needs.

Labor & Employee Relations

  • Serve as a key HR partner for a workforce that includes both union-represented and non-union employees.
  • Provide day-to-day labor relations guidance and counsel to leaders and managers regarding interpretation and application of collective bargaining agreements, workplace policies, practices, and employment requirements.
  • Manage and support the grievance process, including investigating concerns, gathering and evaluating relevant information, advising management, preparing responses, and partnering with Employee Relations and Legal as appropriate.
  • Build and maintain productive working relationships with union representatives while balancing employee, business, and organizational needs.
  • Participate in and support labor negotiations, requiring demonstrated negotiation skills and the ability to prepare for and navigate complex labor discussions.
  • Support contract administration and the consistent application of collective bargaining agreement provisions.
  • Partner with leaders on employee relations matters involving performance, attendance, conduct, conflict resolution, workplace investigations, and policy interpretation.
  • Coach managers on effective employee relations practices and appropriate documentation.
  • Identify potential employee and labor relations risks and escalate significant compliance, litigation, or business risks to Employee Relations, Legal, or senior HR leadership as appropriate.
  • Promote fair, consistent, and compliant employment practices across union and non-union employee populations.

Organizational Effectiveness & Change Management

  • Support organizational design and workforce structure initiatives aligned with business priorities.
  • Advise and coach leaders through organizational change, restructures, workforce transitions, and evolving operating models.
  • Develop and implement change management approaches that support effective communication, employee understanding, and adoption.
  • Assess organizational and employee trends and recommend solutions that strengthen engagement, effectiveness, and performance.
  • Partner with leaders and HR colleagues to support a positive employee experience during periods of change.

Workforce Planning & Talent Strategy

  • Partner with leaders to assess current and future workforce requirements and identify talent and capability needs.
  • Support workforce planning activities to align staffing, skills, and organizational capabilities with business objectives.
  • Partner with Talent Acquisition on hiring strategies and workforce needs.
  • Support talent reviews, succession planning, and development planning for key roles and employee populations.
  • Identify talent risks and opportunities and work with leaders to develop appropriate action plans.

Talent Management & Leadership Development

  • Facilitate and support performance management, talent review, and employee development processes.
  • Coach managers and leaders to strengthen leadership capability, team effectiveness, and employee performance.
  • Partner with Talent Development and other HR Centers of Excellence to implement programs that build critical workforce and leadership capabilities.
  • Advise leaders on performance improvement, employee development, retention, and career planning.
  • Support managers in addressing complex employee performance and conduct matters.

Engagement, Culture & Inclusion

  • Partner with leaders to foster a high-performance, inclusive, and engaging workplace aligned with company values.
  • Support employee engagement initiatives, including employee survey analysis and action planning.
  • Identify workforce trends and recommend actions to strengthen employee engagement, retention, and organizational health.
  • Partner with leaders and HR colleagues to promote inclusive talent and employment practices.
  • Support fair and consistent application of compensation and reward practices in partnership with Total Rewards.
  • Build trusted relationships across union and non-union employee populations and promote constructive employee-management relationships.

HR Programs, Compliance & Continuous Improvement

  • Implement HR programs, policies, frameworks, and tools in alignment with business requirements and enterprise HR practices.
  • Ensure HR practices comply with applicable employment and labor requirements, company policies, and collective bargaining agreements.
  • Lead or contribute to HR projects and initiatives that improve organizational effectiveness and employee experience.
  • Identify opportunities to improve HR processes, tools, and ways of working.
  • Partner effectively across HR, Employee Relations, Legal, Compliance, and business teams to resolve complex workforce matters.
  • Maintain current knowledge of HR practices, employment and labor relations trends, and evolving HR technologies.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of progressive Human Resources experience, with significant experience operating as an HR Business Partner, HR Manager, or comparable role in a complex organization.
  • Bachelor's degree in human resources, Business, Organizational Development, Labor Relations, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience will be considered.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting union-represented employees is required.
  • Demonstrated experience handling employee and labor relations matters, including grievances, investigations, performance, conduct, and workplace concerns.
  • Strong negotiation skills and experience working effectively with union representatives and management.
  • Experience interpreting and administering collective bargaining agreements.
  • Experience participating in union/collective bargaining agreement negotiations is preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to support both union and non-union employee populations.
  • Experience advising and coaching managers on complex HR and employee relations matters.
  • Demonstrated experience with organizational change, performance management, workforce planning, and talent management.
  • Strong understanding of employment practices, labor relations principles, and HR compliance requirements.
  • Strong business acumen with the ability to connect people priorities to operational and business outcomes.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to use workforce data and insights to identify trends and recommend solutions.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication, interpersonal, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence, build credibility, and establish trusted relationships across multiple levels of an organization.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, manage sensitive and confidential matters, and navigate complex employee situations.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and HR initiatives in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
  • Demonstrated use of AI and HR technology to improve effectiveness, productivity, and employee or manager experiences.
  • Curiosity and commitment to continuous learning and improvement.

jobs.description:
About The Position

The Senior Manager, People Products and Systems designs, builds, and continuously improves the products, processes, and data systems that power KIPP Foundation's talent strategy.

This role is responsible for transforming complex talent work into simple, scalable experiences for KIPP Foundation staff. The Senior Manager owns a portfolio of talent products across the employee lifecycle, including tools, templates, workflows, dashboards, documentation, and operating processes. They partner closely with the People Operations, Data and Analytics, and Marketing and Communications teams to ensure talent systems are intuitive, data-driven, and consistently executed across the organization.

The ideal candidate is an exceptional systems thinker who enjoys bringing order to complexity. They are equally comfortable designing new processes, analyzing data, documenting workflows, facilitating stakeholder conversations, and improving products based on user feedback.

Responsibilities

Product Management

  • Own the lifecycle of multiple Development and Management Cycle products such as Core Skills Rubric and related toolkits, from discovery through implementation and continuous improvement.

  • Translate organizational strategy into practical tools, templates, dashboards, workflows, and resources.

  • Gather user feedback and analyze usage data to prioritize product improvements that allow for user friendliness and impact.

  • Define product requirements and partner across teams to deliver high-quality solutions.

  • Maintain a product roadmap that balances strategic priorities with operational needs.

Process Design & Continuous Improvement

  • Design, document, and continuously improve talent processes that increase consistency, efficiency, and user experience.

  • Build repeatable systems that reduce complexity and enable high-quality execution across the organization.

  • Identify bottlenecks, root causes, and opportunities for automation or simplification.

  • Ensure processes align with organizational operating norms and integrate effectively with adjacent systems.

Data & Insights

  • Develop and maintain reliable data systems that support talent decisions.

  • Partner with stakeholders to define meaningful success metrics and dashboards.

  • Monitor data quality and establish processes that ensure accuracy and consistency.

  • Translate quantitative and qualitative data into actionable insights that inform strategic decisions.

Project & Change Management

  • Lead cross-functional implementation of new products and processes.

  • Create project plans, monitor milestones, and proactively manage risks.

  • Develop communications, training, and implementation resources that support adoption.

  • Build stakeholder investment through thoughtful change management.

Knowledge Management

  • Create and maintain clear documentation for products, systems, and processes.

  • Ensure institutional knowledge is organized, accessible, and continuously updated.

  • Establish standards for documentation, version control, and process ownership.

Skills and Mindsets

  • Mission and Student Focus: Demonstrates passion and commitment to KIPP’s mission and possesses the desire and ability to uphold KIPP’s core values (Focus on Excellent Results, Collective Impact, and Courageous Action)

  • Self Management: Demonstrated record of co-creating ambitious goals with their managers – and driving toward desired outcomes; Effectively monitors progress toward goals for multiple workstreams; Leverages understanding of an organization’s operating model, structure, and core operational process to effectively drive work to achieve goals; effectively works through direct reports and peers to follow through on commitments, ensuring others do the same

  • Continuous Learning: Engages in the work of personal development at work, knowing that personal development is ongoing and vital to their personal and professional success; hold themself accountable to evolving, growing, learning, and unlearning in ways that improve results for students, adults, and the larger community.

  • Process Management: Able to build and align goals and project plans with organization priorities; leverages relevant organizational processes and systems to execute work; can build and maintain knowledge management systems; effectively develops and codifies processes to ensure efficiency, alignment with organizational processes, and to improve work quality.

  • Problem Solving: Generates solutions outside of their direct work and shrinks problems to solve independently. Shows initiative in generating and recommending ideas and solutions within their own workstreams. Anticipates risks and develops proactive solutions that support their team.

  • Collaboration: Leads successful stakeholder management, accounting for varied perspectives when gathering feedback. Builds coalition by prioritizing end-user experiences. Builds trusting relationships and effective communications. Able to identify and remove barriers to working across teams.

Experience and Qualifications

  • 5+ years of work experience and results with creating and implementing talent processes and tools, especially in the development, performance management, and employee recognition.

  • Experience in the K-12 sector is strongly preferred, but not mandatory

  • Experience providing services at an organization with national reach and working with teammates across multiple time zones

  • Microsoft Office Experience (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)

Work Conditions

  • Travel: up to 10% (3-4 times per year)

  • Full, exempt role

Location

It is preferred, but not mandatory for this role to be based out of a KIPP Foundation office. This role has the option of working from a remote office full-time. KIPP Foundation offices are in NYC and Chicago.

Compensation and Benefits

In compliance with local law, we are disclosing the compensation, or a range thereof, for roles in locations where legally required. Actual salaries will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, and relevant experience. The salary range for this position is $104,000-123,500. In addition, KIPP Foundation provides a variety of benefits to employees, including: 

  • 25 holidays for + 18 days additional flexible PTO days (flexible PTO increases to 23 days for years 3 and 4 and to 28 days for years 5+).

  • 100% paid parental leave

  • 100% coverage of the premium for employee and 75% for employee + family’s medical/dental/vision plans.

  • Wellness benefits such as fitness reimbursements, discounted tickets to theme parks/attractions, backup care support for children and adults/elders, and our employee assistance program

  • Finance Security benefits include such as a 401K retirement plan with 4% match, employer-sponsored legal plans, life/disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts

KIPP Foundation embraces the opportunity to build a workforce that reflects the diversity of the students and communities with whom we work and the world that’s around them. Being an equal opportunity employer means that we take seriously our responsibility to consider qualified candidates on the basis of merit, without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, mental or physical disability, and genetic information, marital status, citizenship status, military status, protected veteran status or any other category protected by law.

About the Organization

KIPP Public Schools is a national network of tuition-free public charter schools that prepares students with the skills and confidence to create the future they want for themselves, their communities, and us all. We are a network of 279 schools, nearly 16,500 educators, and nearly 210,000 students and alumni.

Our mission: Together with families and communities, we create joyful, academically excellent schools that prepare students with the skills and confidence to pursue the paths they choose—college, career, and beyond—so they can lead fulfilling lives and build a more just world.

Our vision: Every child grows up free to create the future they want for themselves and their communities.

The KIPP Foundation is a nonprofit organization that supports KIPP public charter schools across the country. The KIPP Foundation helps to develop outstanding educators to lead KIPP schools; provides tools and resources for excellent teaching and learning; promotes innovation; and facilitates the exchange of insights and ideas across KIPP and other public schools and organizations.

About Our Values:

Excellent Results for Students: We value results over effort and know that our work is not finished until all students thrive. We maintain high expectations for self, team, and students. We drive outcomes by operating with agility, removing barriers, differentiating support, and prioritizing student-centered solutions—especially for those at the margins.

Collective Impact: We are one team. We win together. We embody a one-team mindset by working collaboratively across teams, aligning goals, and leveraging the strengths of all teammates. We build trust-based relationships and ensure inclusive decision-making by engaging those closest to the work. We provide clarity through simple, repeatable systems and goals that enable transformational outcomes.

Courageous Action: Our belief in what we can achieve is unwavering, fueling our optimism and commitment to overcome any challenge. We demonstrate an unwavering belief in students' potential and a commitment to addressing systemic inequities. We approach challenges with resilience, a solutions-focused mindset, and adaptability. We foster a psychologically safe environment centered on trust and accountability where feedback is encouraged. We leverage data to reflect on progress, own setbacks, celebrate successes, and continuously improve to maximize impact.

  • Conduct a test purchase to validate the full checkout and fulfillment flow

FBM and FBT Configuration

  • Configure FBM: Set warehouse / pickup and return addresses; create shipping templates covering rates, zones, and carrier selection
  • Configure FBT: enroll products, prepare inbound shipments to TikTok warehouses, and configure the free-shipping opt-in settings
  • If using Shopify: install and configure the TikTok channel app to enable real-time inventory and order sync
  • Author and publish the shop's return policy in compliance with applicable consumer protection laws
  • Draft 3PL to FBT ongoing inventory management plan and workflow.

Customer Service

  • Configure customer service notifications
  • Set up FAQs, saved responses, and response workflows
  • Establish return, refund, and cancellation handling procedures
  • Set escalation path for customer support issues

Advertising & Promotions Setup

  • Link TikTok Ads Manager to the shop and configure the primary ad account
  • Launch initial GMV Max campaign(s) — set target ROI, daily budget, and product selection
  • Set up TikTok Search Ads with relevant keyword targeting to capture intent-driven discovery
  • Configure TikTok Pixel if driving traffic to an external website or landing page
  • Build out and maintain welcome promotions, platform coupons, and launch discount strategies in Seller Center

Affiliate / Creator Program Setup

  • Enable and configure the Affiliate Center, including open and targeted collaboration plans
  • Work with our Affiliate/Creator team to set baseline and tiered commission structures across product categories
  • Work with our Affiliate/Creator team to establish a product seeding / free sample program and write a creator brief with content guidelines

PHASE 2 RESPONSIBILITIES — ONGOING MANAGEMENT & OPERATIONS

Daily Operations

  • Monitor and respond to all buyer messages within 12 hours
  • Verify the processing and fulfillment of new orders
  • Review and action open return and refund requests in line with shop policy
  • Monitor product and video comments for customer questions, complaints, or escalations
  • Check the Shop Health dashboard daily for violations, warnings, or Late Dispatch Rate (LDR) increases

Weekly Operations

  • Review GMV Max campaign performance (cost, orders, CPA, ROI) and adjust target ROI as needed
  • Audit GMV Max creative assets and exclude under-performing videos
  • Review inventory levels and initiate restock for SKUs approaching low thresholds
  • Sync inventory counts across all sales channels to prevent overselling
  • Review Search Ads keyword performance and refine bids and match types
  • Monitor and respond to product reviews; flag patterns requiring action
  • Update product listings as needed: pricing, imagery, descriptions, or promotional badges

Monthly Operations

  • Produce a full performance report covering GMV, orders, ad spend, ROAS, and affiliate ROI
  • Export raw order data and build a net revenue / P&L analysis — accounting for referral fees, transaction fees, affiliate commissions, and fulfillment costs
  • Reconcile payouts against Seller Center invoices
  • Review TikTok's ACE Powered Insights for platform-generated growth recommendations
  • Analyze SKU-level performance and identify top and bottom performers
  • Plan and schedule upcoming promotions, flash sales, and seasonal campaigns
  • Work with our Affiliate/Creator Team to review and adjust affiliate commission rates; roll out performance bonuses for top creators
  • Review FBT warehouse inventory and plan replenishment inbound shipments
  • Conduct a shop health audit covering seller score, policy compliance, and LDR trends
  • Monitor TikTok platform policy updates, fee changes, and new ad format rollouts

Quarterly / Strategic Operations

  • Set and document measurable growth goals for the upcoming quarter in collaboration with stakeholders
  • Evaluate catalog expansion opportunities: new SKUs, product bundles, or virtual bundles
  • Review and optimize the fulfillment strategy mix (FBT vs. seller-ship vs. 3PL)
  • Audit the full technology and integration stack: inventory sync tools, shipping apps, analytics platforms
  • Evaluate eligibility for premium seller tiers including Star Shop and Mall status

Crisis & Issue Management

  • Triage and respond to Shop Health violations — pause campaigns and slow order intake if LDR spikes
  • Conduct root cause analysis for fulfillment failures or policy incidents and implement corrective action
  • File TikTok support tickets with supporting documentation when external factors are responsible
  • Manage chargebacks, fraud disputes, and escalated return or refund claims

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE & SKILLS

Platform & Technical

  • Proven hands-on experience managing a TikTok Shop end-to-end via Seller Center — from initial registration through to active daily management
  • Deep familiarity with TikTok Shop Ads — specifically GMV Max campaign setup, optimization, and creative management
  • Working knowledge of Fulfilled by TikTok (FBT): inbound shipping, warehouse management, and fee structures
  • Experience with TikTok Shop's affiliate and creator program: collaboration setup, commission structures, and creator relationship management
  • Proficiency with TikTok Seller Center tools: Shop Health dashboard, ACE Powered Insights, order management, and promotions
  • Experience integrating TikTok Shop with Shopify or other e-commerce platforms for catalog and inventory sync
  • Familiarity with TikTok Search Ads and keyword-based campaign strategy

Operations & Analytics

  • Strong understanding of TikTok Shop's fee structure — referral fees, transaction fees, FBT costs, affiliate commissions, and refund admin fees
  • Ability to build and interpret P&L analyses and net revenue reports from raw Seller Center order data
  • Experience managing customer service operations within a 12-hour response SLA
  • Comfortable managing inventory across multiple fulfillment channels and preventing overselling

Soft Skills & Working Style

  • Highly organized and process-driven — able to manage multiple daily, weekly, and monthly operational rhythms simultaneously
  • Proactive communicator — surfaces issues, opportunities, and insights to stakeholders without prompting
  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving platform environment where policies and features change frequently
  • Detail-oriented with a strong compliance mindset around TikTok's evolving seller policies

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • In the first 30 days: The shop is fully configured, the product catalog is live and approved, fulfillment is operational, the GMV Max campaign is running, and the affiliate program is open for creator applications.
  • By 90 days: The shop has an active roster of affiliate creators generating content, ad campaigns have been optimized based on real performance data, and a regular reporting cadence is in place.
  • Ongoing: The shop maintains a healthy seller score, a sub-12-hour message response rate, and a consistent upward GMV trend quarter-over-quarter.

jobs.description:
This is a fractional role with an hourly rate, ideal for an experienced leader who wants to bring their expertise, network, and executive presence to a growing team.

The Company

At Servant, we specialize in empowering leaders and organizations within faith communities through innovative digital transformation and change management solutions. We are dedicated to providing tailored strategies that align with our clients' values and missions, focusing on service, integrity, and excellence. Our team is passionate about driving impactful change by equipping our partners with the tools and technologies they need to thrive in a digital age.

Position Overview

Servant is seeking an experienced AI Delivery Engine Leader to design and build the next generation of our delivery organization. This leader will architect an AI-first operating model that transforms how ideas move from strategy to production—leveraging AI agents, automation, orchestration, and modern software delivery patterns to dramatically increase speed, quality, and scalability.

The vision is to create a highly automated delivery engine capable of taking ideas from concept through implementation with minimal human intervention where appropriate. While a fully autonomous ("dark factory") model remains an aspirational future state, this role will establish the practical AI factory model that allows small, highly capable teams to deliver work that traditionally required significantly larger organizations.

This individual will work directly with executive leadership to define the architecture, operating model, tooling ecosystem, governance, and implementation roadmap required to modernize Servant's delivery capabilities. They will bridge strategy and execution, bringing deep technical expertise while helping the organization adopt practical AI-enabled ways of working.

Key Responsibilities

Design the AI Delivery Engine

  • Architect Servant's AI-first delivery operating model from strategy through implementation and ongoing support.
  • Define the workflows, orchestration patterns, automation, and governance required to create a highly efficient AI-enabled delivery organization.
  • Develop repeatable delivery frameworks that leverage AI agents throughout the software development lifecycle.
  • Create scalable processes that reduce manual effort while maintaining quality, security, and reliability.

Build the AI Factory

  • Design and implement an AI "factory" capable of moving ideas from concept to production through integrated AI workflows.
  • Identify where humans remain essential versus where AI can own or significantly accelerate execution.
  • Evaluate opportunities to automate planning, requirements generation, architecture, coding, testing, documentation, deployment, monitoring, and support.
  • Establish delivery patterns that enable smaller, highly effective project teams without compromising outcomes.

Drive Technical Transformation

  • Evaluate emerging AI platforms, agent frameworks, orchestration tools, and delivery technologies.
  • Recommend and implement the tooling ecosystem required to support an AI-first organization.
  • Partner with engineering, product, strategy, and delivery leaders to modernize existing processes.
  • Bring external perspective from organizations that have successfully implemented AI-enabled delivery models.

Lead Organizational Change

  • Assess current delivery processes and identify opportunities to simplify, automate, or eliminate unnecessary work.
  • Help define new roles, responsibilities, and operating rhythms within an AI-enabled organization.
  • Guide leaders through organizational change while balancing innovation with practical execution.
  • Establish metrics to measure speed, quality, utilization, automation, and delivery effectiveness.

Serve as an Executive Partner

  • Act as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on AI strategy and delivery transformation.
  • Translate emerging AI capabilities into practical business value.
  • Build a phased roadmap toward increasingly autonomous delivery capabilities.
  • Help shape Servant's long-term vision for AI-enabled consulting and software development.

Requirements

Ideal Experience

We're looking for someone who has helped build AI-enabled delivery organizations—not simply experimented with AI tools.

The ideal candidate has:

  • Deep technical experience in AI systems, LLMs, agent frameworks, orchestration platforms, and modern software architecture.
  • Experience designing AI-first software delivery workflows or "AI factory" operating models.
  • A track record of transforming engineering organizations through automation and AI.
  • Experience implementing AI across multiple phases of the software development lifecycle.
  • Strong understanding of DevOps, CI/CD, automated testing, infrastructure automation, and platform engineering.
  • Experience evaluating and integrating emerging AI technologies into enterprise environments.
  • Ability to balance strategic vision with hands-on execution.
  • Exceptional communication skills with both executive and technical audiences.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity while building new organizational capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience implementing AI delivery models across multiple organizations.
  • Background in software consulting or professional services.
  • Experience leading cross-functional transformation initiatives.
  • Familiarity with AI agent orchestration frameworks and autonomous workflow systems.
  • Experience building or operating highly automated engineering organizations.
  • Understanding of governance, security, and responsible AI implementation.

jobs.description:
About Us
Original Composites and Fibers is a global leader in glass reinforcement solutions for the composites industry. Recently separated from Owens Corning, the business now operates independently under the Praana ownership model, continuing a strong legacy of innovation, manufacturing excellence, and customer partnership.

With more than 4,000 employees worldwide, we are committed to redefining what's possible through a performance-driven culture centered on safety, quality, sustainability, inclusiveness, and employee development. Guided by our values of passion, ownership, and team spirit, we work together to deliver innovative solutions and exceptional service across the globe.

About the Role
We are seeking a skilled Information Technology (IT) SAP Supply Chain Professional with strong expertise in one or more of the SAP S/4HANA Supply Chain solutions, including Extended Warehouse Management (EWM), Transportation Management (TM), Integrated Business Planning (IBP), Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling (PP/DS), Production Planning (PP), Materials Management (MM), Inventory Management, Logistics Execution, Global Trade Services (GTS) and related SAP supply chain technologies within an SAP S/4HANA RISE Cloud Private Edition environment.

The ideal candidate combines strong SAP application knowledge with business process understanding and the ability to guide business stakeholders, implementation partners, and technical teams toward scalable, fit-to-standard, future-ready SAP solutions. This role will help establish consistent global processes across demand planning, supply planning, production planning, warehouse operations, transportation management, inventory management, logistics execution, order fulfillment, and supply chain reporting.

Original Composites & Fiberglass is a business unit of the Praana Group. Original Composites & Fiberglass was recently acquired by the Praana Group. The path ahead will be dynamic, full of change, and expected to be fast paced. The business operates from twenty (20+) locations across the globe. The information technology environment supporting our new company is being built from the ground up in terms of IT infrastructure and applications with the opportunity to leverage new technologies and new ways of thinking as we look to end a transition services agreement associated with the acquisition as soon as possible. Our Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) landscape is comprised of multiple instances across the globe. We seek to consolidate and simplify our ERP landscape to drive efficiency and effectiveness in our operations for decades ahead.

All IT team members may be assigned IT Engineering responsibilities, focused on designing, building, and maintaining technology systems that support business operations. These assignments ensure secure connectivity, scalable platforms, and reliable data flow to enable efficient supply chain operations and enterprise-wide digital transformation, especially during the separation from Owens Corning. Roles may be temporary or ongoing and can include direct ownership of IT service delivery.

Key Responsibilities
  • Work hands-on in the functional design, configuration, testing, and delivery of SAP Supply Chain solutions across SAP S/4HANA, EWM, TM, IBP, PP/DS, PP, MM, Inventory Management, and Logistics Execution, while prioritizing SAP-delivered capabilities, best practices, fit-to-standard principles, and clean core design approaches.
  • Provide IT supply chain expertise and guidance to business stakeholders by translating planning, manufacturing, warehousing, transportation, inventory, logistics, and fulfillment requirements into practical SAP solution designs that support global manufacturing operations.
  • Drive standardization and simplification of global supply chain processes, including demand planning, supply planning, production planning, inventory management, warehouse operations, transportation planning, logistics execution, order fulfillment, global trade compliance, and reporting standards.
  • Understand and support integrations between SAP S/4HANA, SAP EWM, SAP TM, SAP IBP, SAP PP/DS, SAP BTP / Integration Suite, manufacturing systems, warehouse automation solutions, transportation carriers, third-party logistics providers, procurement systems, customer service platforms, and other third-party supply chain applications.
  • Support data migration, supply chain master data readiness, cutover planning, mock conversion testing, user acceptance testing, defect resolution, hyper care, and stabilization activities for SAP S/4HANA deployment waves.
IT Engineering (As Assigned)
  • Own IT service delivery for assigned business organizations, maintaining strong relationships and ensuring operational excellence.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to deliver IT services aligned with business needs during organizational transitions, including separation activities.
  • Participate in the design and implementation of secure, scalable, and reliable technology solutions that support core business operations and digital transformation.
  • Ensure supply chain data integrity and seamless data flow across enterprise systems, enabling efficient planning, manufacturing, logistics, warehouse operations, transportation execution, inventory visibility, reporting, and compliance activities including trade compliance and regulatory reporting requirments.
Skills & Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Operations Management, or related field, or equivalent work experience.
  • 8 to 10 years of experience in SAP Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Logistics, Planning, Warehouse Management, Transportation Management, or enterprise application roles.
  • Experience with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, RISE with SAP, SAP S/4HANA migration, and greenfield deployment projects preferred but not required.
  • Strong knowledge of Demand Planning, Supply Planning, Material Requirements Planning, Production Planning, Detailed Scheduling, Inventory Management, Warehouse Management, Transportation Management, Logistics Execution, Order Fulfillment, Manufacturing Operations, and Supply Chain Reporting processes.
  • Proven experience implementing enterprise supply chain platforms in global manufacturing environments, preferably across multiple countries, business units, and ERP instances.
  • Strong understanding and hands-on experience with supply chain master data governance, data quality, migration, and business data structures supporting planning, transportation, warehousing, manufacturing, and logistics execution processes.
  • Functional experience in one or more SAP Supply Chain solutions, including SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM), SAP Transportation Management (TM), SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP), SAP Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling (PP/DS), SAP Global Trade Service (GTS) and SAP Available-to-Promise (aATP).
Work Conditions
  • Potential 20% travel required.
  • Due to the team structure, virtual meeting formats, time zone differences, and appropriate meeting times, extended work hours may be required.

Executive Assistant to the C-Level
Remote — Central Time required (Texas preferred) | Dance background required
Full-Time Regular | Corporate | Reports to the CEOLocationRemote (U.S.) — Texas strongly preferred; must work Central Time hoursReports ToChief Executive OfficerDepartmentCorporateEmployment TypeFull-Time Regular, Non-ExemptScheduleMonday–Friday, core business hours Central Time; occasional evenings and weekends around events and travelTravelOccasional, up to 15% (events, leadership meetings, partner visits)PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING
1. You live and work on Central Time. Texas is strongly preferred. This role runs the CEO's day in real time, so you must be available during core Central business hours — not shifted from another time zone.
2. You come from the dance world. You have competed, trained, taught, choreographed, worked at a studio, or worked events and conventions in dance. You know how this industry works and can speak its language with our partners from day one.ABOUT DANCEONE
DanceOne is the leading platform for world-class dance events and experiences. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Los Angeles, DanceOne is the largest holding company of dance brands in the world — home to Ovation, Jump, NUVO, 24 Seven, RADIX, KĀOS, Starpower, NexStar, Revolution, Believe, Imagine and DreamMaker, alongside events including DancerPalooza, PowerPak, The DanceOne Summit and the World Dance Championship.
We serve hundreds of thousands of dancers each year and hold ourselves to the highest possible safeguarding standards, so that every dancer has a safe environment in which to learn. Our teams work cross-functionally across Corporate, Tours, Production, Warehouse and Driver operations — a genuinely collaborative environment built on a shared passion for the work.POSITION SUMMARY
The Executive Assistant to the CEO is the operational right hand to DanceOne's Chief Executive Officer — owning the calendar, inbox and travel so the CEO's time goes to the highest-value work. Beyond core executive support, this role is a partner-facing extension of the CEO's office: maintaining the partnership contact list and mailing calendar, driving follow-ups to completion after every meeting, and preparing the CEO ahead of each conversation with the context and read of the room needed to walk in ready. This is a role for someone who anticipates rather than reacts and who is comfortable holding confidential information. Two things are required, not preferred: you work on Central Time (Texas preferred), and you come from the dance world — as a competitor, dancer, teacher, studio or event professional. We are not looking for someone who will learn this industry on the job; we are looking for someone who already understands who is in the room and why it matters.ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Manage the CEO's calendar. Own scheduling end to end across multiple time zones — booking, confirming, protecting time, resolving conflicts and reprioritizing as the week changes.
  • Run the inbox. Triage incoming email, draft and send correspondence on the CEO's behalf, flag what needs a decision, and make sure nothing waiting on the CEO goes quiet.
  • Coordinate travel and logistics. Build detailed itineraries for flights, hotels, ground transport and on-site event schedules, and adjust in real time when plans change.
  • Prepare the CEO for every meeting. Assemble pre-meeting briefs covering who is attending, relationship history, open items and the outcome we want — so the CEO walks in with a read on the room.
  • Own partnership mailings. Maintain the partner and sponsor contact database, and build, proof and send partnership communications, announcements and seasonal outreach on schedule and on brand.
  • Drive follow-ups to closure. Capture action items from CEO meetings, route them to the right owners, track them in a shared tracker and chase them until they are done.
  • Serve as a first point of contact. Represent the office of the CEO with partners, sponsors, studio owners, vendors and internal leaders — warmly, professionally and with sound judgment about what to escalate.
  • Prepare materials and support leadership meetings. Build agendas, decks, pre-reads and reports to an external-ready standard; coordinate executive and cross-brand meetings and offsites, take minutes and publish decisions and next steps.
  • Process expenses and invoices. Prepare the CEO's expense reports, reconcile receipts, and route partner invoices and contracts to Finance.
  • Support events as needed. Assist with on-site logistics, VIP and partner hospitality, and CEO scheduling at DanceOne events and conventions.
  • Perform additional duties using Artificial Intelligence - as assigned.
QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
  • Three or more years of experience as an Executive Assistant, Administrative Coordinator or similar, supporting a senior executive.
  • Dance industry background required. Meaningful firsthand experience in dance — as a competitive or pre-professional dancer, studio owner or staff member, choreographer, teacher, or event and convention staff. You know how the studio, competition and convention world works and can speak its language credibly with partners.
  • Based in the United States and able to work core business hours in the Central Time zone; Texas strongly preferred.
  • Proven track record managing a complex, changing executive calendar across multiple time zones.
  • Excellent written communication; able to draft polished, on-brand correspondence on an executive's behalf.
  • Proficient with Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams) and comfortable learning new systems quickly.
  • Demonstrated discretion handling confidential information.
  • Reliable high-speed internet, a professional remote workspace, and availability for occasional evening, weekend and event travel.
PREFERRED
  • Experience supporting a founder or CEO at a high-growth or multi-brand company, and with partnership, sponsorship or client-relationship communications.
  • Familiarity with CRM, email marketing and project management tools (HubSpot, Salesforce, Mailchimp, Asana, Notion or similar).
SKILLS & COMPETENCIES
  • Anticipation. Sees what the CEO will need before being asked and prepares it.
  • Relationship instinct. Reads people and situations well, and knows how to prepare an executive for the room they are walking into.
  • Follow-through and precision. Nothing falls through the cracks; open loops get closed without reminders, and the typo, wrong date or double-booking gets caught first.
  • Organization under pressure. Juggles competing priorities calmly during peak event season.
  • Judgment and discretion. Knows what to handle independently, what to escalate and when to say no on the CEO's behalf, and holds sensitive personnel, financial, partnership and safeguarding information in complete confidence.
  • Self-direction. Thrives working remotely with minimal supervision and stays visible and responsive.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORK ENVIRONMENT
  • Primarily a remote, sedentary office role: extended periods seated at a computer, with frequent use of a keyboard, monitor and phone, and clear communication by phone, video and email throughout the business day.
  • Occasional travel by air and car; event environments include loud music, crowds, extended time on foot, long days and occasional lifting up to 25 pounds.
  • Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role.
OUR CULTURE COMES FIRST — THE G-I-F-T-S OF DANCE
  • Gratitude. We lead with appreciation — for each other, for our dancers and community, and for the opportunity to do meaningful work.
  • Innovation. We embrace change and challenge the status quo. We believe innovation drives growth, excellence and impact.
  • Fun. We bring joy to everything we do. Fun energizes our teams and strengthens our connections.
  • Trust. Trust empowers us to collaborate, take risks and support one another — on and off the dance floor.
  • Safety. We put safety first — always. We create environments where dancers, employees and spectators feel secure and supported.
BENEFITS & PERKS
  • Medical, Dental and Vision;
  • Health Savings Account employer contribution, and Flexible Spending Accounts for healthcare and dependent care.
  • 401(k) with a 4% company match - eligible after three months.
  • Group and Voluntary Life and AD&D coverage, and an Employee Assistance Program.
  • Paid time off, employee discounts and the InsurChoice voluntary benefits program. Coverage begins the first of the month following your date of hire.
WHY JOIN DANCEONE
This is a seat at the center of the largest dance company in the world. You will work directly with the CEO, see how a multi-brand business runs from the inside, and build relationships with the partners and studio leaders who shape the industry. If you grew up in dance, this role keeps you in the room where it happens.

jobs.title: Director, Growth
jobs.excerpt: The Director, Growth will be responsible for leading BayNova’s end-to-end Federal proposal development lifecycle while serving as a key leader within the company’s growth organization.
jobs.description:
The Director, Growth will be responsible for leading BayNova’s end-to-end Federal proposal development lifecycle while serving as a key leader within the company’s growth organization. This role will ensure BayNova consistently submits high-quality, compliant, and compelling proposals while helping mature the people, processes, tools, and content that support sustainable business growth across Federal Civilian, Health, and DoW markets.

Proposal leadership is the primary responsibility of this role and represents the company’s highest growth priority. The Director, Growth is expected to balance broader growth initiatives with the timely delivery of winning proposals, ensuring proposal excellence remains the primary focus of the role.

The Director, Growth works closely with executive leadership, BD/Capture/Sales, technical subject matter experts, delivery teams, partners, and subcontractors to translate customer requirements into winning proposals. Beyond proposal leadership, the role contributes to capture planning, market research, marketing initiatives, customer engagement planning, corporate capabilities development, and continuous improvement of the company’s growth processes.

This position reports directly to executive leadership and plays a critical role in achieving the company’s strategic growth objectives.

This is a remote position.

Role Priorities

While this position contributes across multiple aspects of the company’s growth organization, responsibilities are prioritized as follows:

  1. Lead the successful development and submission of winning proposals.
  2. Develop and mature the proposal infrastructure, tools, reusable content, and processes that improve long-term growth effectiveness.
  3. Support business development, capture, marketing, and delivery activities where those efforts directly strengthen active pursuits or position the company for future opportunities.

As the company grows, the scope of this role may expand to include broader ownership of growth operations and/or leadership of additional growth personnel.

Key Responsibilities

Proposal Leadership (Primary Responsibility)

  • Lead the complete proposal lifecycle (RFIs, Sources Soughts, RFP, RFQs, etc.) from opportunity qualification through submission and post-submission lessons learned
  • Write Technical, Management, Past Performance and other sections as needed to respond to customer requirements
  • Develop proposal schedules, compliance matrices, outlines, storyboards, and production plans.
  • Manage proposal teams consisting of technical/delivery staff, pricing, contracts, recruiting, and executive leadership.
  • Drive proposal strategy, win themes, discriminators, messaging, and customer-focused content.
  • Ensure proposal compliance with solicitation requirements, evaluation criteria, and submission instructions.
  • Coordinate color team reviews (Pink, Red, Gold, White Glove) and ensure timely incorporation of reviewer feedback.
  • Oversee proposal production, quality assurance, formatting, graphics coordination, and final submission.
  • Maintain proposal repositories, templates, boilerplate content, resumes, past performance libraries, and proposal knowledge management assets.
  • Analyze proposal metrics and implement continuous process improvements to increase proposal quality and win rates.

Business Development & Capture Support

  • Partner with business development personnel to qualify opportunities aligned with company strategy.
  • Assess opportunities posted to eBuy, SAM.gov, etc. and provide pursuit recommendations.
  • Participate in bid/no-bid decisions.
  • Support capture planning activities including competitive analysis, customer research, teaming strategies, and win strategy development.
  • Assist in developing executive summaries, capability statements, and customer presentation materials.
  • Coordinate with teaming partners throughout capture and proposal efforts.
  • Help maintain visibility into the opportunity pipeline to support proposal planning and resource forecasting.

Marketing & Corporate Communications

  • Collaborate on the development of corporate capabilities materials, solution briefs, white papers, case studies, and other customer-facing content.
  • Support marketing initiatives that directly enable business development and proposal efforts. Ownership of broader corporate marketing activities may reside elsewhere within the organization as the company grows.
  • Help maintain corporate messaging, differentiators, and solution positioning.
  • Coordinate announcements related to contract awards, certifications, partnerships, and company achievements, as appropriate.

Delivery & Operations Collaboration

  • Coordinate with delivery leadership to identify reusable technical content, past performance, and staffing resources.
  • Capture lessons learned from project execution to strengthen future proposals.
  • Support transition activities between proposal and program startup when required.
  • Assist with customer presentations, oral proposals, and technical demonstrations.

Growth Process Management

  • Continuously improve the company’s proposal and growth processes, templates, tools, and knowledge repositories, prioritizing initiatives that directly improve proposal quality, efficiency, and win probability.
  • Track key growth metrics including proposal throughput, submission quality, win rate, and proposal resource utilization.
  • Develop and maintain reusable proposal assets, including templates, graphics, standard language, proposal checklists, and knowledge repositories.
  • Own the company’s past performance repository, resume library, and proposal content management strategy.
  • Evaluate and implement AI-assisted proposal development tools and workflows that improve proposal quality and team productivity.
  • Recommend process improvements and automation opportunities that enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of proposal operations.
  • Support strategic planning and annual growth initiatives.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.
  • 8+ years of experience supporting Federal Government proposal management, capture, business development, or growth operations.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex Federal proposals under FAR-based procurements.
  • Strong understanding of Federal proposal best practices, compliance management, and proposal review methodologies.
  • Experience supporting opportunities across Federal Civilian agencies and/or the Department of Defense.
  • Excellent written, editing, and verbal communication skills.
  • Exceptional organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities.
  • Strong leadership and collaboration skills with cross-functional teams.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and proposal collaboration tools.

Preferred

  • APMP Foundation, Practitioner, or Professional Certification.
  • Experience supporting digital modernization, low-code platforms, AI, cloud, cybersecurity, or enterprise IT services.
  • Experience with GSA MAS, GWACs, BPAs, IDIQs, and task order competitions.
  • Familiarity with Shipley proposal methodologies.
  • Experience supporting oral presentations and demonstrations.
  • Experience implementing AI-assisted proposal development or knowledge management solutions.

Desired Characteristics

The successful candidate is both a strategic thinker and a hands-on executor who enjoys building repeatable processes while delivering exceptional proposals under demanding deadlines. They thrive in an entrepreneurial environment, are comfortable wearing multiple hats, and understand how to balance immediate revenue-generating priorities with longer-term investments in growth capabilities.

They are collaborative, highly organized, customer-focused, and continuously seek opportunities to improve the effectiveness of the company’s growth organization through better processes, tools, content, and teamwork.

Success Measures

Success in this role will be measured by:

  • Consistent delivery of high-quality, compliant, and compelling proposals submitted on time.
  • Increased proposal win rates and overall proposal effectiveness.
  • Continuous improvement of proposal operations, reusable assets, and growth infrastructure.
  • Effective collaboration across business development, capture, delivery, marketing, and executive leadership.
  • Development of scalable proposal processes and AI-enabled capabilities that improve efficiency over time.
  • Meaningful contributions to the company’s long-term growth strategy while maintaining proposal excellence as the highest operational priority.

jobs.title: Senior Content & Video Manager
jobs.excerpt: About UsWild Alaskan Company’s mission is to accelerate humanity’s transition to sustainable food systems by fostering meaningful, interconnected relationships between human beings, wild seafood and the planet.
jobs.description:
About Us

Wild Alaskan Company’s mission is to accelerate humanity’s transition to sustainable food systems by fostering meaningful, interconnected relationships between human beings, wild seafood and the planet.

We deliver wild-caught, sustainable seafood to households across the United States. Powered by our custom-built eCommerce platform and three generations of history and expertise in the Alaskan fishing industry, we constantly strive to meet our promise of a top-notch product and experience. And we do it all in a fully-remote environment that is fast-paced, challenging, and fun.

GENERAL ROLE DESCRIPTION

We’re hiring a storyteller to build a long-form video channel that makes people hungry, leaves them longing for Alaska (whether they’ve been there or not), and, every so often, moves them to tears. This is a development-first role but with good working knowledge in production and management. You'll spend more time finding stories, researching them, discovering new culinary trends than deep in production logistics. You need to know the whole production process, as you'll be responsible for it end to end but we are not hiring just a pair of hands. We're hiring for a point of view. This role reports to our VP of Creative and Brand.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Finding and developing the stories. What it takes to come back for a third season on an Alaska fishing boat. Follow the next generation fisherperson as she takes over her family’s setnet site. Follow a chef host as they put the secrets to perfectly crispy skin to the test. You'll build and maintain a real pipeline of story leads, pitch them with a clear vision and argument for why each one matters towards channel and brand growth and easily move on from the ones that don't earn their place.
  • Pre-interviews and research. Long phone calls before anyone books a flight. Do the research, know a subject's history, their vocabulary, the thing they're proud of and the thing they don't usually talk about. Walking into a shoot with a question no one else would have thought to ask.
  • Setting up production for success. Find the right crew, work with multiple producers, create scope, learn to schedule around tides and fishing openers, directing in the field, guiding the edit, delivering on schedule. You'll do some of this yourself, work with content operations and hire out the rest. You'll know when a piece needs a full crew and when it needs one person with a camera and two days of patience—must be flexible towards ideas based on budget.
  • Building the long-form channel and distributing across short form channels. Programming a slate, not posting videos. You will be responsible for series architecture, release cadence, thumbnails and titles that are on brand and perform on YouTube. You will oversee a Social Media Manager and be accountable for the channel's growth and successful articulation of the brand, and you'll have real opinions about how to get it there.
  • Managing a content team. An Editorial Content Producer and a Social Media Manager report to you. Your job is to give them clear content direction, unblock them, defend their good work, learn from them as much as help them get better. Guide their productions, distribution strategies and presentations.
  • Drive performance-minded creative that is worth watching. You’ll lead ideation and review for not just long form video but also paid ad video, bringing a sharp point of view on hooks, storytelling, pacing and brand. You’ll know what makes people stop, watch and act on both conversion and engagement content channels. You use performance to make the creative better, not just more optimized.
  • Making the food look like it tastes. About half of the content we make has a seafood culinary focus. Beyond content around Alaskan lifestyle, you need genuine range to cover: content that shows appetite appeal, working with culinary personalities to keep viewers attention span—the goal here is both useful and inspiring food content.
  • Protecting the brand. We're a company built on dedication and reverence for wild-caught fish from Alaska; we take inspiration from the place it’s from, the hard working people who provide it and thanks for the plates it ends up on— this doesn't need embellishing, just real celebration.. You'll be one of the loudest voices in the room about what's true to that and what isn't.

What Success Looks Like

  • A long-form channel with real, compounding audience growth — subscribers who came for one film and stayed for the next.
  • A story pipeline deep enough that we're choosing between good options, not scrambling.
  • Two direct reports doing the best work of their careers.
  • The team watches a rough cut and gets hungry. Then, about four minutes later, gets a little choked up. We tell stories that make Alaskans proud.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • 7+ years in content, documentary, or brand film. Titles vary; the reel is what matters. Ability to deliver.
  • Experience reviewing creative data around organic and paid social channels.
  • A body of work with at least one deeply character-driven piece you developed yourself, from lead to delivery.
  • Demonstrated management experience. Not "led freelancers" — actual direct reports, reviews, growth.
  • Fluency across two worlds: the outdoors and food. You’re as comfortable around commercial fishing boats, rough weather and working waterfronts as you are in kitchens, with chefs and thinking about appetite. Direct experience in either world is a plus. Most candidates are strong in one. We need someone who can speak both languages.
  • Real understanding of long-form platform mechanics like YouTube. You can talk about viewership metrics and launch strategies.
  • Willing and able to travel often. Alaska in bad weather and test kitchens within the same quarter. Expect roughly 30% travel, weighted heavily toward the summer.
  • Full working knowledge of the production stack: research and development process, budgets, crew, camera, audio, post, color, sound, delivery. You don't have to touch all of it. You have to be un-bluffable about all of it.
  • Who this isn’t for: If your only experience is primarily execution on someone else’s ideas — this is the wrong role, and you'd be unhappy in it. We have great production partners and are looking for more. What we don't have is someone whose ideas are the reason the work exists.

What to include in your application:

  1. A reel. Required. A cut piece or a link to three finished projects, with a line on each telling us specifically what was yours: the idea, the development, the direction, the edit.
  2. One page on a story you developed from nothing. How you found it, what you learned in pre-interviews that changed your approach, and what you'd do differently.
  3. Three pitches for us. One character-driven, one culinary, one your call. A paragraph each. We're not looking for polish, we're looking for what you notice.

The starting salary range for this position is $125,000 - $130,000, commensurate with skills and experience. Wild Alaskan’s benefits package includes health, vision, and dental insurance, 401k, PTO, safe/sick time, vacation, parental leave and more, as well as a delicious box of free fish every month.

Wild Alaskan participates in E-Verify. Please see the Notice of E-Verify Participation and Right to Work posters for more information.

Diversity of backgrounds and perspectives makes us stronger. We’re committed to creating a work environment that fosters growth, celebrates diversity and fundamentally makes all teammates feel welcome, accepted, nurtured and respected. An overview of this role

GitLab’s Security Assurance organization is responsible for how GitLab designs, tests, and evidences the controls that protect the business. This role operates the technology compliance program across the systems that run the company, and is deliberately framework- and department-agnostic: the same control discipline applies wherever a system is material to financial reporting, security commitments, customer contracts, or regulatory obligations. In scope are IT-owned corporate applications and identity infrastructure, Corporate Security tooling, Engineering-owned applications that support business operations (usage-based billing, subscription and entitlement tracking, metering, provisioning), and third-party SaaS where GitLab retains control responsibility.

SOX ITGC is one driver of this work, not the whole of it. You will design a control once and satisfy multiple assurance consumers from the same evidence. You will also support corporate security policy work in partnership with the Security Governance team, and help set standards for the governed use of AI across the corporate and business-systems estate.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Building a control set for an Engineering-owned billing or subscription system that satisfies SOX ITGC, SOC 2, and customer contractual commitments from a single body of evidence.
  • Setting the standard for how AI tools, agents, and integrations are used in corporate and business systems — what acceptable use looks like, what evidence is required, and when a use case needs Legal, Privacy, or Internal Audit review.
  • Automating recurring evidence collection so access reviews and change-management testing stop being a manual quarterly scramble.

What you’ll do

  • Design, document, and maintain IT General Controls and security controls across the in-scope estate, and test them for design and operating effectiveness against regulatory, contractual, and corporate policy requirements.

  • Serve as the compliance point of contact and liaison for the IT, Corporate Security, Engineering, and Finance teams that own in-scope systems, so a single assessment serves Security Governance, Security Risk, Internal Audit, the SOX PMO, Legal, and Privacy.
  • Help set standards and control expectations for the governed use of AI across corporate and business systems — assess tools, agents, and integrations for control impact, define what acceptable use and evidence look like, and escalate where a use case is SOX-relevant or touches customer data.
  • Partner with Security Governance on corporate security policy work: contribute and review policy, standard, and procedure content for the systems you act as liaison for, and support policy review, attestation, and Acceptable Use Policy adherence.
  • Run recurring compliance monitoring — user access reviews, privileged access, segregation of duties, change management, and configuration baselines — on monthly, quarterly, and annual cadences.
  • Assess system implementations, migrations, and significant changes for control readiness ahead of go-live, and advise Engineering and application teams on control requirements early in design.
  • Manage SOX ITGC testing and certification requests from internal and external auditors, and direct evidence collection for external audits, automating that collection wherever possible.
  • Identify, track, and lead remediation of control deficiencies and risks, and recommend improvements to compliance processes, metrics, and reporting across the estate.

What you’ll bring

  • 5+ years in IT compliance, security compliance, IT audit, information security, or information technology, with a BA/BS in a business or technology field or equivalent experience. Big 4 or external audit experience is a plus.
  • Demonstrated experience testing controls and documenting those tests against frameworks such as COSO, COBIT, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2, and SOX ITGC, and working directly with internal or external auditors.
  • Experience assessing controls in SaaS and cloud-native application stacks, not only traditional on-premise systems.
  • Working knowledge of identity and access management — SSO, SCIM, RBAC, privileged access, and joiner/mover/leaver processes.
  • Familiarity with AI governance concepts and the control questions raised by AI tools, agents, and integrations — data handling, access scope, human review, logging, and evidence.
  • Experience contributing to security policies and standards, and supporting policy adherence or attestation processes, in partnership with a governance function.
  • Ability to reason about how data flows between product usage, billing, subscription, and financial reporting systems, and where control risk sits in those flows.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, with demonstrated credibility across senior leadership, engineering teams, auditors, and legal.
  • Ability to use GitLab, or willingness to learn.
  • Nice to haves: Relevant certifications such as CISA, CISSP, CRISC, or CISM; experience with usage-based or consumption billing platforms, subscription management systems, or in-house metering and entitlement services; experience with compliance automation and continuous control monitoring, or setting standards for AI use in an enterprise environment (ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF); prior experience in a Security Assurance or GRC function that supported both corporate IT and product engineering.

TheSecurity Assurance organization helps GitLab build and maintain trust by strengthening how we approach security, compliance, and risk across the company.
